subject: Human Evolution
title: Parasites and Co-Evolution
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Parasites and Co-Evolution.

hook.text: Hookworms have lived in human guts for millions of years. They evolved alongside us, finely tuned.

buildup.text: Parasites that kill their host too fast die with it. The most successful ones keep you alive—barely.

discovery.text: Our immune system evolved partly in response to this constant parasitic pressure over millions of years.

twist.text: In parasite-free modern environments, the immune system attacks harmless things—allergies and autoimmunity.

climax.text: Some researchers deliberately reintroduce hookworms to treat Crohn's disease—with promising results.

punchline.text: We evolved to be infected. Clean living confused our immunity.

quiz.question: How does the 'hygiene hypothesis' relate to parasites?
options: Lack of parasites may trigger allergies and autoimmune disorders
